[USER] There is a non-standard drive on the target machine. Find it, and then locate the flag.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To find the non-standard drive on the target machine, you can use the command "wmic logicaldisk get name, description" in the command prompt.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] This will display a list of all the drives on the machine, including the non-standard drive.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Once you have located the non-standard drive, you can navigate to it and search for the flag.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If you know the name of the file or directory that the flag is in, you can use the "dir" command to search for it.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If you are not sure where the flag is located, you can use the "dir /s" command to search the entire drive for the flag.  
[USER] Which drive on the target machine contains the CD-ROM?  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The drive letter for the CD-ROM on a Windows machine is typically D: or E:.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] However, it can vary depending on the configuration of the computer and the number of other drives present.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To check which drive is the CD-ROM on a Windows machine, you can use the command "wmic logicaldisk get name, drivetype" in the command prompt.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] This command will list all the drives on the machine and their drive types. Drive type 5 corresponds to CD-ROM.
